payload.prompt: Which statements correctly describe speech recognition, also called STT?

options.rationale: Speech recognition is the ability to detect and interpret spoken input. That is why it is used when audio needs to be understood.
Speech recognition converts spoken words into data, usually text. This makes the audio usable for captions, transcripts, or notes.

options.rationale: Apps can respond to audio after spoken words are converted into data. Speech recognition provides that input step.

options.text: It generates audible speech from text
options.error_type: confuses STT with TTS
options.rationale: Generating audible speech from text is speech synthesis. Speech recognition goes the other way, from spoken input to text-like data.
options.better_fit: This would fit text-to-speech, where written content is read aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The learner would choose a speaking capability when the task needs listening.
feedback.instructional: STT starts with speech and usually ends with text; TTS starts with text and ends with speech.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. STT detects spoken input and usually turns it into text data that an app can use.

payload.prompt: Which statements correctly describe speech synthesis, also called TTS?

options.rationale: Speech synthesis is the ability to generate spoken output. It is used when an app needs to speak to a person.

Reading messages aloud is a common use of speech synthesis. The message text becomes audible speech.

options.error_type: confuses TTS with STT
options.rationale: Detecting spoken input is speech recognition. Speech synthesis creates spoken output instead.
options.better_fit: This would fit speech recognition, where an app listens to spoken words and converts them to text.

feedback.intrinsic: The learner would choose a listening capability when the task needs speaking.
feedback.instructional: TTS is the output direction: it turns text-based data into audible speech.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. TTS starts from text-based data and generates spoken output, such as reading messages aloud.
